subtype: Approach: getting used to water in the shallow end first [Thinking]
passage: Every Saturday I watch the new boy in our swim class, Uday, stand at the pool's edge with his arms folded. Today he stepped down to where the water reached only his knees and stayed there, splashing a little with one hand. I heard him mutter, "If I'm okay here, maybe up to my waist. If that's okay, then floating." He said it like a list. His face looked stiff, maybe scared, maybe just cold, I can't tell. After ten minutes he splashed with both hands and even laughed, once, quickly. The coach didn't push him. I told him "nice" and he nodded without looking at me. - Tenzin

What does Uday's muttered list suggest about how he is handling his fear?
qa.a: It suggests he calms himself by taking one small step at a time and feeling safe before moving on, though his stiff face shows some fear stayed.

qa.q: What other approach could help Uday reach the floating step, and why?
qa.a: He could practise floating while the coach stands close and steadies him, so the next step comes with help and grows gradually.

qa.a: Tenzin cannot tell whether the stiff face meant fear or cold, but notices the laugh and stays quiet, seeing a slow, brave beginning.

grounding: A boy afraid of water starts in the shallow end and reasons that feeling safe there leads to the next step.

subtype: Approach: getting used to water in the shallow end first [Thinking]
passage:
Monday: Noor stood at the edge of the club pool, gripping the rail. His sister Dilnaz was already in. "Just the steps," she said. Noor sat on the top step with his feet in and his heart hammering.
Thursday: He walked down into the shallow end, where the water only reached his waist. He splashed. He scooped water onto his arms. "If I can stand here and feel okay," he thought, "then next time I can try lying back." The coach nodded from the side.
Saturday: He stood in the shallow end, took a breath, and leaned back into the coach's hands. For two seconds, he floated. He sat up spluttering and grinning. "Again."

qa.q: How deep was the water where Noor stood on Thursday?
qa.a: The water only reached his waist.

qa.q: How was Noor feeling on Monday, sitting on the top step?
qa.a: He was scared, with his heart hammering, though he still put his feet in.

qa.q: What else could help Noor after floating with the coach's hands, and why?
qa.a: He could hold the side and practise putting his face in the water, because each small step keeps the fear from getting big again.

qa.q: How does Noor's progress look to Dilnaz?
qa.a: Dilnaz sees her brother go from gripping the rail to floating in a week, so she is probably happy and proud.

grounding: It shows a boy afraid of water starting in the shallow end, reasoning that feeling safe there lets him try floating next.

subtype: Approach: getting used to water in the shallow end first [Thinking]
passage: Vidya, beti, you don't want to go to swimming class because the water scares you? Sit. Your Nilesh Dada was the same. We lived by a river, and every boy in the village could swim except me. They'd dive off the rock, and I'd sit on the bank. One day my uncle said, "Don't start with the rock. Start where the water is at your knees." So I did. I stood in the shallows and splashed, day after day, until my heart stopped jumping. I told myself: if I feel safe here, I'll go to my waist. Then I did. Then I learnt to float with him holding me. I never dived off that rock, beti. But I swam, and he was always nearby.

qa.q: Where did Nilesh's uncle tell him to start?
qa.a: His uncle told him to start where the water was at his knees.

qa.q: How did young Nilesh feel sitting on the bank while the others dived?
qa.a: Young Nilesh felt scared and probably left out, since every other boy could swim.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story, and why did it work?
qa.a: Starting in the knee-deep shallows was the turning point, because feeling safe there made each next step possible.

qa.q: How might Nilesh's uncle have seen the slow progress?
qa.a: The uncle likely felt patient and proud, watching the boy grow braver step by step while staying nearby.

grounding: An elder recalls being a boy afraid of water, starting in the shallows until he felt safe and then moving on to floating.
